title: Natural selection causes extinction of less improved forms and divergence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural selection causes extinction of less improved forms and divergence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Natural selection almost inevitably causes much extinction of less improved forms of life and produces divergence of character.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we shall then see how Natural Selection almost inevitably causes much Extinction of the less improved forms of life and induces what I have called Divergence of Character.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), the Introduction; section “Introduction”. Scope: all organic beings over evolutionary time

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-intro-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Divergence and extinction are measurable, but 'less improved' requires substantial reinterpretation. Fossil and phylogenetic data support restricted tests, not the claimed near-inevitability or attribution to selection.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use time-calibrated phylogenies and fossils to test whether lineage divergence is associated with inferred selection and whether less-adapted lineages have elevated extinction. Patterns must exceed neutral diversification and environmental-turnover null models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Diversification models have identifiability problems.

Fitness of extinct forms is usually unobserved.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.58

discriminating power: 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Extinction tallies and disparity curves are standard products of open fossil and tree databases, so the pattern half can be examined for well-skeletonized groups. Linking those patterns specifically to selection, rather than to environmental forcing or sampling, needs a fitness measure the occurrence tables do not contain. The analysis is feasible for marine animals and much weaker for the full scope of organic beings.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure genus- and species-level extinction rates and morphological disparity through time in the fossil record, and sister-lineage trait divergence on time-calibrated trees. The pattern side would be supported if less persistent forms disappear while disparity among survivors grows; attributing both patterns to natural selection would require a fitness proxy that outpredicts abiotic drivers.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Preservation bias truncates last occurrences and inflates late Cenozoic diversity.

'Less improved' has no direct fossil measurement and is easily confused with rarity or short stratigraphic range.

Mass extinctions, climate, and sampling intensity produce extinction and apparent divergence without a selection mechanism.
